title: Digital Media, Genetics, and Risk for ADHD Symptoms in Children: A Longitudinal Study
authors: Nivins S, Mooney MA, Nigg J, Klingberg T

primary_models.name: Linear mixed model of repeated CBCL ADHD symptom scores (T0-T4) on 4-year average social media use and social media use x time, adjusted for age, sex, SES, PGS-ADHD and 10 genetic PCs
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 2, top panel (Social Media Use rows), p. 6; Results text p. 5 ('DM Use and ADHD-Related Symptoms'); interpreted in Discussion p. 7.
primary_models.design: Longitudinal cohort, ABCD baseline (T0, ages 9-10) and four annual follow-ups (T1-T4). The outcome enters as repeated measures at T0-T4 (not averaged), with random intercepts and slopes. The exposure is a single time-invariant value per child: average daily social media hours across all available visits (T0-T4), chosen by the authors to absorb the COVID-19-era increase in use. The focal longitudinal term is the two-way social media use x time interaction (described by the authors as the between-person longitudinal effect, i.e. difference in yearly symptom slope); the social media main effect is the association with symptom level at time = 0. A three-way social media use x time x PGS-ADHD term tests genetic moderation of the slope. Because the exposure is averaged over the same waves as the outcome, IV and DV are not strictly temporally ordered.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Data Release 5.0. Of 11,875 enrolled children, 8,324 included at T0 after excluding children born extremely preterm (<28 weeks), birthweight <1200 g, not English-proficient, neurological problems, history of seizures, or MRI contraindication, and keeping one randomly selected child per family. Follow-up >85% through T3 and 43% at T4. Mean age at T0 9.9 (SD 0.6); 4,408 (53.0%) male. Race/ethnicity: White 4,356 (52.3%), Black 1,358 (16.3%), Hispanic 1,763 (21.2%), Asian 496 (6.0%), Native American 183 (2.2%), Pacific Islander 2 (0.02%), Other 106 (1.3%). N = 8,324 printed in Table 2 header for all cells.
primary_models.iv: Social media use, a phone/SM-only composite from the youth-reported Youth Screen Time Survey: item 4 (texting on a cell phone, tablet, or computer, e.g. Google Chat, WhatsApp) + item 5 (visiting social networking sites, e.g. Facebook, Instagram) + item 6 (video chat, e.g. Skype, FaceTime). Daily hours = [(weekday hours x 5) + (weekend hours x 2)]/7, then averaged across T0-T4. Average over 4 years: mean 1.4 (SD 1.0) hours/day (Table 1). By wave: T0 0.5 (1.1), T1 0.9 (1.6), T2 1.3 (1.4), T3 1.9 (1.5), T4 2.5 (1.4) hours/day. Coefficients are reported as standardized betas.
primary_models.dv: Parent-reported CBCL ADHD symptoms at every visit, as three continuous scores run in separate models: (1) combined ADHD = CBCL DSM-5-oriented ADHD scale raw score (cbcl_scr_dsm5_adhd; alpha > 0.72 at all time points); (2) inattention = 4 CBCL items retained by factor analysis (loading > 0.3) of the 9 DSM-5 ADHD items, correlated r = 0.93 with the CBCL inattention summary score at T0; (3) hyperactivity-impulsivity = 5 items from the same factor analysis. T0 means (SD): combined 2.7 (3.0), inattention 1.7 (1.9), hyperactivity-impulsivity 1.3 (1.8) (Table 1). Raw item sums, not T-scores.

covariates.name: Time
covariates.detail: Visit (T0-T4), entered as fixed effect and in interaction with social media use

covariates.name: Socioeconomic status
covariates.detail: First principal component of parental education, household income, and neighborhood quality; Table 1 mean 0.03 (SD 1.4)

covariates.name: PGS-ADHD
covariates.detail: Polygenic score from the 2016-2017 PGC + iPSYCH ADHD GWAS (LDpred), standardized to mean 0, SD 1; also enters the three-way interaction

covariates.name: Genetic principal components
covariates.detail: First 10 genetic PCs, for ancestry/genetic confounding

primary_models.equation: ADHD_DV[i,t] = b0 + b1*SM_avg[i] + b2*time[t] + b3*SM_avg[i]*time[t] + b4*age_T0[i] + b5*sex[i] + b6*SES[i] + b7*PGS_ADHD[i] + b8*SM_avg[i]*time[t]*PGS_ADHD[i] (with lower-order terms) + b9..b18*genPC1-10[i] + u_site + u0_i + u1_i*time[t] + e[i,t]. Focal: b3 (SM x time); b1 (SM level) and b8 (genetic moderation) also printed.
primary_models.estimation: R 3.5 (RStudio), lmer in lme4, restricted maximum likelihood. Random intercepts and slopes; study site as random effect. Separate model per DM category (social media, video games, TV/videos) and per symptom score (combined, inattention, hyperactivity-impulsivity). Coefficients reported as standardized beta (SE); no CIs or exact p-values printed in Table 2. Alpha 0.05 with Bonferroni correction for 9 tests (0.05/9 = 0.005); Table 2 footnotes mark a = <0.001 and b = <0.005 (Bonferroni corrected). Authors define yearly standardized beta > 0.05 or cumulative beta > 0.10 as meaningful. Moderation of significant DM x time effects by sex, ADHD diagnosis at T0, and ADHD medication at T0 tested in separate models (Supplemental Tables 1-3, not bundled in the PDF; reported non-significant). Sensitivity analyses (at-term births only; typically developing children only; complete behavioral data only; follow-up truncated at T3) reported narratively as consistent (Supplemental Tables 4-8, not bundled).

primary_models.name: Linear regression of 4-year change in inattention symptoms (T4-T0) on average social media use, adjusted for predefined covariates (cumulative effect)
primary_models.location_in_paper: Results p. 5 ('Cumulative Effect Size of DM Use on ADHD-Related Symptoms (T4-T0)'); Figure 2B (p. 6); interpreted in Discussion p. 7 ('cumulative effect over the study period was 0.15'); details in Methods in Supplemental Material (not bundled).
primary_models.design: Longitudinal change-score analysis. DV is the single difference score in inattention from baseline (T0) to 4-year follow-up (T4); IV is average social media use across T0-T4. One observation per child. Authors present this as the cumulative 4-year effect corresponding to the yearly SM x time slope in M1, and anchor their population-level interpretation (0.15 SD) to it.
primary_models.sample: Same ABCD Release 5.0 cohort as M1 (N = 8,324 at T0). The analytic N for the T4-T0 change score is not printed; T4 follow-up was 43%, so the effective N is likely considerably smaller than 8,324.
primary_models.iv: Average daily social media use (texting + social networking sites + video chat) across T0-T4, hours/day; mean 1.4 (SD 1.0) (Table 1). For Figure 2B the authors split it into quartiles (Q1 <0.54, Q2 >=0.54 to <1.36, Q3 >=1.36 to <1.86, Q4 >=1.86 hours/day in the panel legend; the Figure 2 caption instead gives cutoffs 0.61, 1.22, 1.97), but the reported beta uses the continuous variable.
primary_models.dv: Change in the 4-item CBCL-derived inattention score from T0 to T4 (T4 minus T0). T0 inattention mean 1.7 (SD 1.9); SD of the change score not reported.

covariates.name: Predefined covariates
covariates.detail: Stated as 'adjusting for predefined covariates (Methods in Supplemental Material)'; presumably the M1 set (age at T0, sex, SES, PGS-ADHD, 10 genetic PCs, site) but the exact list is in the unbundled supplement

primary_models.equation: Inattention_T4[i] - Inattention_T0[i] = b0 + b1*SM_avg[i] + covariates[i] + e[i]. Focal: b1.
primary_models.estimation: R 3.5 (RStudio). Regression class and estimator not specified in the main text beyond 'regressing total change'; whether site enters as random effect is not stated. Standardized beta (SE) and p reported. Meaningfulness threshold: cumulative beta > 0.10. Cumulative effects for video games and TV/videos on hyperactivity-impulsivity change are also reported in text (excluded below). Cumulative effects of social media on combined ADHD or hyperactivity-impulsivity change are not reported.

primary_models.name: Cross-lagged panel model of social media use and inattention symptoms across T0-T4 (standardized paths)
primary_models.location_in_paper: Figure 3 (p. 7); Results text p. 6 ('Additional Analyses'); Discussion p. 7; Methods in Supplemental Material (not bundled).
primary_models.design: Five-wave cross-lagged panel model (T0-T4) with autoregressive paths for inattention (delta1-4 = 0.75, 0.74, 0.74, 0.74) and social media use (alpha1-4 = 0.42, 0.46, 0.55, 0.56), within-wave covariances at T0 and T4 drawn, and cross-lagged paths in both directions. The cross-lagged paths are displayed with identical values at every lag (gamma = 0.03 for S(t) -> I(t+1); beta = -0.002 for I(t) -> S(t+1)), suggesting equality constraints across lags. Social media is the IV in the S -> I path and the DV in the I -> S path.
primary_models.sample: ABCD Release 5.0 cohort as in M1 (N = 8,324 at T0); handling of missing waves (e.g., FIML) and analytic N not stated in the main text.
primary_models.iv: Wave-specific social media use (texting + social networking sites + video chat), hours/day, at T0-T3 for the S -> I paths. Wave means (SD): T0 0.5 (1.1), T1 0.9 (1.6), T2 1.3 (1.4), T3 1.9 (1.5), T4 2.5 (1.4). For the reverse path, wave-specific inattention is the IV.
primary_models.dv: Wave-specific inattention (4 CBCL items) at T1-T4 for S -> I; wave-specific social media use at T1-T4 for I -> S.

covariates.name: Not reported in main text
covariates.detail: Covariates for the CLPM are described only in the unbundled supplemental methods

primary_models.equation: I[t+1] = delta_t*I[t] + gamma*S[t] + e_I[t+1]; S[t+1] = alpha_t*S[t] + beta*I[t] + e_S[t+1], t = 0..3; cov(I0,S0) and cov(e_I4,e_S4) estimated. Focal: gamma (S -> I) and beta (I -> S).
primary_models.estimation: Cross-lagged panel model; software beyond R 3.5 and estimator not specified in main text. All coefficients standardized beta weights. Figure 3 marks a = P < .01, b = P < .001; text gives exact p for the cross-lagged paths.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: Standardized beta treated as approximate r: d = 2*beta_std / sqrt(1 - beta_std^2) (guidelines section 4a).
d_transformation.contrast_type: Per 1 SD of social media use (hours/day) in SD units of the symptom score; for M1 SM x time terms, per 1 SD of average social media use difference in the yearly symptom slope; for M2, per 1 SD of average social media use in the 4-year inattention change score.
d_transformation.notes: All estimates are reported as standardized betas, so SD_IV and SD_DV are not needed for conversion. SDs recorded for reference from Table 1 (pp. 4-5): average social media use over 4 years 1.0 h/day; T0 combined ADHD 3.0, inattention 1.9, hyperactivity-impulsivity 1.8. Convertible: M1 social media main effects, M2 cumulative beta 0.15, M3 cross-lagged paths, M4 reverse paths (SM as DV). Caveats: (1) the M1 SM x time coefficients are differences in yearly slope, so a d derived from them is a per-year rate, not a level difference, and is not comparable to cross-sectional d's; (2) the three-way SM x time x PGS-ADHD terms are moderation effects and should not be converted; (3) how the authors standardized variables inside lmer (both sides z-scored vs. partial standardization) is not described; (4) only SEs are reported, no CIs, so d CIs cannot be formed without computing beta +/- 1.96*SE, which the extraction rules prohibit. The M4 total effect has no SE or p.

extraction_flags:
1. The supplement is not bundled in the 10-page PDF. As a result, the M2 cumulative-change covariates, the CLPM (M3) covariates, missing-data handling and estimator, the full M4 reverse-direction spec, Supplemental Tables 1-8 (moderation and sensitivity analyses) and analytic Ns other than 8,324 could not be checked.
2. The 'social media use' IV is a composite of texting, social networking sites and video chat (YSTS items 4+5+6). All three items are phone/SM, so it qualifies under Step 2. Texting is asked as cell phone/tablet/computer, which is activity-defined and qualifies under clarification 5.
3. The exposure is averaged over T0-T4, the same waves as the outcome, so the IV and DV are not temporally ordered in M1 and M2.
4. In M1 the authors anchor on the SM x time interaction, which gives a difference in yearly slope. A d derived from it is a per-year rate. I included the three-way SM x time x PGS-ADHD terms as estimates and flagged them as not convertible; a coder may prefer to strike them.
5. Table 2 prints only beta (SE) with Bonferroni footnote markers. Cells without a marker are coded sig=false with p null. CIs are null throughout and the SEs are in the notes.
6. In M3 the CLPM cross-lagged values look constrained equal across lags; this is inferred from the figure.
7. The M4 total effect (-0.01) has no SE or p. sig=false is set only because no test is reported.
8. The Figure 2 caption quartile cutoffs (0.61/1.22/1.97) disagree with the Figure 2B panel legend (0.54/1.36/1.86).
9. The year is recorded as 2025 per items.json, but the journal issue is Vol 2, Issue 1, 2026.
10. Spot-checked all 9 Table 2 social media cells plus the in-text values 0.15, 0.03/p=.004, -0.002/p=.64 and -0.01/SE 0.001 against the PDF text layer; all match.
